title: Security checks
request: Confirm with tests, and add any that are missing: a strict CSP with no outside host and no inline code, the CSRF token on every write, the host check, upload names that cannot leave the draft's folder, no secret in any draft, event, response or error, and an accurate statement of what a model may read.
spec: The strict CSP, the CSRF token on every write, the host check, sanitised upload names, and no secret in any draft, event or response. Done when the web build, agentic, connectors and draft-flow tests pass.
plan: Check the CSP names no outside host and allows no inline code (tests in test_web_build).
Check every write route refuses a request without the CSRF token and a request with another Host header is refused.
Check an upload's file name cannot leave the draft's data folder, for drafts and projects.
Check no key, token or connection string appears in drafts, events, responses or errors (connector tests).
Check that what the Admin page says a model may read matches the code.

decisions.decision: The CSP lists no outside host at all after the fonts were self-hosted.
decisions.why: Every page load stays on the machine.

decisions.decision: The privacy text names each path that sends data to a model (the intern's example values, the parse pattern's sample lines).
decisions.why: A privacy promise must be exactly as strong as the code.

change: Tests across test_web_build, test_agentic, test_connectors and test_draft_flow; studio.data.safe_name used by every upload route; the privacy text corrected.

findings.defect: Project uploads never sanitised the file name, so '../x' could write outside the project's data folder.
findings.scenario: The project upload route called studio.data.safe_name only if it existed; it did not exist under that name, so a file named '../x' was written outside the data folder.
findings.cause: A defensive call guarded by 'if present' silently did nothing.
findings.fix: safe_name now exists, strips paths and unsafe characters, rejects an empty name, and the route calls it directly.
findings.test: tests/test_studio.py uploads ../evil.csv to a project and tests/test_draft_flow.py uploads ../../tickets.csv to a draft; both land inside the data folder.

findings.defect: The privacy statements were stronger than the code.
findings.scenario: The Admin page and /api/config said rows never reach a model, while the intern sends up to three example values per column and an unparseable file sends up to 20 lines to work out its format.
findings.cause: Texts written for one agent were not updated as paths were added.
findings.fix: Both paths are named in the privacy text; the line sending can be switched off with DCLAB_MODEL_READS_SAMPLE_LINES=0.

outcome: Done: the listed protections are tested; the upload traversal is closed; the privacy text matches the code.
lessons: A security call wrapped in 'if the helper exists' is a silent no-op waiting to happen; call it directly and let a missing helper fail loudly.
